question.text: During a SIAB hearing into alleged professional misconduct by an empanelled SIA, the aggrieved SIA is entitled to:

answer.text: Written charges, a fair hearing, the right to lead evidence, the right to cross-examine witnesses and the right to be represented by a qualified professional.
A private in-camera hearing only if the charges relate to money-laundering, otherwise the SIA has no right to personal appearance.
A 7-day hearing window with no right to lead evidence - only to submit a written reply.
Only a right to submit a written reply; the SIAB panel's determination is ex-parte by default.

explanation.text: The Logic: Principles of natural justice - embedded in ICAI disciplinary jurisprudence and SIAB's scheme - require: written charges (audi alteram partem), fair hearing, right to lead evidence, right to cross-examine witnesses, and right to be represented by counsel or a qualified peer. The Trap: Ex-parte default, reply-only proceedings and narrow in-camera rules defeat natural justice. Candidates sometimes confuse SIAB with an informal SRO committee - it is a quasi-judicial disciplinary body. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C tests ICAI Council disciplinary rights; XXIII brings the same to SIAB. Assessor's Pro-Tip: If representing a fellow SIA under disciplinary enquiry, insist on a witness list at the show-cause stage. Surprise witnesses at hearing are grounds for adjournment. Cross-examination of the complainant's principal witness usually determines the outcome.
